claim: IC3 complaints whose text references AI: losses
metric: Losses in complaints with 'AI Related' descriptor
ai_role: Mention-based: 'information reported contains a reference to artificial intelligence'; covers AI-written messages, cloned voices, deepfake videos, 'AI trading' pitches, and victims' guesses
but_for_judgement: Mostly NOT but-for: the descriptor marks AI presence, not causation; the same investment/BEC/romance schemes ran at large scale pre-2023. Plausible AI-caused uplift is a fraction of this (<<$0.9bn). Upper bound on victim-noticed AI involvement, not on AI-caused loss; lower bound on AI presence (victims often cannot tell).
source_title: FBI IC3 2025 Internet Crime Report (AI section, pp.42-43; Appendix B)
notes: 22,364 complaints; first year captured (2023-24 'not captured'). Verified this session. [Published 2026-04.]

claim: Deloitte projects gen-AI could enable US fraud losses of $40bn by 2027
metric: Projected US fraud losses 'enabled' by gen AI
ai_role: Projection: 'generative AI fraud risk' scores assigned to each of 26 IC3 fraud types plus assumed growth rates under conservative/base/aggressive adoption
but_for_judgement: Not a but-for estimate: the $12.3bn 2023 base is essentially total IC3-type fraud (IC3 2023 total $12.5bn), i.e. losses in AI-susceptible categories, not AI-caused losses. Implied path 2025 ~$21bn ~= IC3 2025 total ($20.9bn), so the 'forecast' is matched by ordinary fraud growth with only 4% AI-mentioning.
source_title: Generative AI is expected to magnify the risk of deepfakes and other fraud in banking (Deloitte Center for Financial Services)
notes: Method: expert judgement; scenario values other than headline not published; BEC aggressive-scenario $11.5bn by 2027. Widely misquoted as 'AI fraud will cost $40bn'.
